How to use this summary

This compact, two-column reference sheet supports quick recall across selected Edexcel GCSE Physics electricity topics. Use it alongside fuller teaching notes and question practice, rather than as a substitute for learning the concepts.

The four pages bring together definitions, circuit symbols, equations, unit conversions, short worked examples, cause-and-effect explanation chains and frequent mistakes. There are no separate exercise sets or answer section.

4 pages · Equation bank · Definitions and explanation chains

Topics covered

  • Page 1: charge, circuit symbols, meters, equations and units
  • Page 2: series and parallel rules, component graphs, sensors and practical methods
  • Page 3: power, energy, kWh, domestic electricity and safety concepts
  • Page 4: static electricity, electric fields, generation, transformers and transmission

A summary of selected electricity content, not a full GCSE Physics revision guide or question workbook. This independent Study with Dr resource is not an official Pearson Edexcel publication. Original diagram attribution is retained. This is not a guide to working on mains wiring; practical work should use teacher-approved low-voltage equipment.

Key ideas at a glance

Use the equation bank with consistent units

The summary collects Q = It, E = QV, V = IR, P = IV, P = I²R and E = Pt. Convert milliamperes to amperes and minutes to seconds before using SI equations.

State the condition that makes a rule true

When predicting current, state whether voltage is constant. For ohmic-resistor behaviour, specify constant temperature. For high-voltage transmission comparisons, specify the same transferred power.

Build an explanation chain

Link cause, process and result rather than listing disconnected keywords. For example, higher transmission voltage at fixed power gives lower current, which reduces I²R cable heating.
